A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SuperMat and contain readable main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Corresponding components and relocated material can be matched reliably despite substantial experimental and methodological additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original material-decomposition and relighting results in Table 1, loss-function experiments in supplementary Table 2, and qualitative 3D reconstruction and ablation results.

after.justification: v4 reports original SuperMat and SuperMatMV results, training-data ablations, quantitative UV-refinement evaluation, and novel-view relighting experiments in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: v1 processes views independently with SuperMat before UV blending and refinement. v4 introduces SuperMatMV, using 3D self-attention and camera-extrinsic conditioning to jointly decompose six views, and incorporates it into the 3D pipeline. This substantially changes cross-view processing; the original single-view architecture and losses remain.

E1.justification: v4 adds Digital Twin Catalog to training and image-space evaluation, retaining Objaverse and BlenderVault. It also introduces StanfordORB and a distinct evaluation of complete 3D objects under novel viewpoints and lighting. Conversely, v1's standalone captured-photograph demonstrations in Figure 14 are removed.

E2.justification: v4 adds StableMaterialMV to Table 1 and the corresponding per-dataset comparisons. All six original baselines remain, so comparator membership expands by one relevant multi-view variant.

E3.justification: Reported SuperMat training changes from 100k to 75k objects, three to sixteen rendered lighting conditions, 115 to 30 epochs, batch size 16 to 32, and learning rate 1e-5 to 2e-5. The re-render lighting pool changes from 716 to 50 maps. v4 also explicitly retrains IIR and RGB→X on its data and introduces a 3D evaluation using 28 objects, 60 novel viewpoints, and three environment maps.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained end-to-end, re-render-loss, and loss-function ablations, v4 adds synthetic-only, real-captured-only, and mixed-data training comparisons in Table 3. Table 4 adds numerical evaluation before and after UV refinement, substantially strengthening v1's qualitative analysis of that component.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and averages without independent-run variability, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional experiments retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main and per-dataset results are extensively revised, with new SuperMatMV and DTC entries. New Table 5 reports pipeline relighting PSNRs of 27.00 on BlenderVault and 24.99 on StanfordORB. Table 2 also changes the loss ranking: perceptual loss leads every metric in v1, whereas L1 leads albedo and metallic SSIM in v4. Changed training and evaluation conditions prevent interpreting revised scores as direct same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: The rendering equation, perceptual and re-render losses, and UV-blending mathematics are retained. The PBR formulation moves from v1 Section 3.1 to v4 supplementary Section 6, with equation renumbering but no substantive mathematical revision or new proof.

C1.justification: The headline claims of state-of-the-art single-step decomposition, millisecond inference, and approximately three-second 3D processing remain. The 3D contribution is refined to explicitly incorporate SuperMatMV and joint cross-view prediction, without changing the paper's overall objectives.

C2.justification: New Section 10 explains limitations involving detail sharpness, inability to obtain alternative predictions by rerunning the deterministic model, and difficulty with transparent, multilayered, or highly reflective materials. v4 also interprets training-data diversity as improving generalization and assigns cross-view consistency more directly to SuperMatMV, emphasizing missing-region completion for UV refinement.

D1.justification: v4 adds a project-page link, the expert branches' parameter overhead, RM-channel conventions, and SuperMatMV initialization and training details, including three epochs with batches of eight six-view inputs. It removes v1's exact VGG feature-layer selection. These are targeted additions and losses of reproducibility information alongside the protocol revisions.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning across material generation, inverse rendering, image decomposition, and UV-space generation. New citations include rendering-aware material estimation, MVDream for multi-view conditioning, and Clay for expert branches, alongside broader generation literature. This changes attribution and contextualization beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The main narrative order and much of the prose remain. v4 rewrites portions of the introduction and related work, moves the PBR subsection into the supplement and training-data description into the main experiments, reorganizes supplementary discussions, and updates terminology and affiliations.

P2.justification: Qualitative comparison grids are extensively rebuilt with paired viewpoints and additional multi-view columns. v4 adds novel-view relighting and DTC figures, removes the captured-photograph gallery, adds three experimental tables, and expands the detailed tables with DTC columns. Figure 2 is relocated, while several existing pipeline and result illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: v1's central 3D-pipeline claim was supported mainly by qualitative examples. v4 adds quantitative ground-truth novel-view relighting comparisons and UV-refinement validation, addressing an important evidential gap. Training-data ablations, explicit baseline retraining, and substantive limitations further improve rigor. These gains outweigh the loss of the captured-photo gallery and exact VGG-layer specification. The improvement rests on stronger validation and clearer boundaries, not on directly comparing aggregate scores obtained under changed settings.
